newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: It was a lethargic day on the local bond market on Monday after sharp moves on Friday as players held stock ahead of the release of key U.S. data on Tuesday and Wednesday.
Government's benchmark R150 stock ended the day slightly higher at a two-and-a-half-month high of 15.31 percent from its previous closing level of 15.28 percent.
"Most people are long ahead of the U.S. CPI numbers tomorrow, just holding positions," a trader at a major foreign institution said.
On Tuesday, the March U.S. consumer price index reading is due for release at 1230 GMT, while U.S. industrial production data is expected at 1315 GMT on Wednesday.
Dealers said the market would look to the data for further clues on whether the Federal Reserve would further tighten U.S. monetary policy at its next meeting on May 20.

The benchmark U.S. 30-year long-bond kicked up to its highest close since July last year on Friday when it rose to 7.17 percent after the release of core March PPI data which traders said pointed to increased chances of a 25 to 50 basis point U.S. rate hike next month.
The U.S. T-bond was trading unchanged in early New York trade on Monday.

Local traders said the 15.31 percent was a key technical level, which some felt signalled the top of the bear run. But others said while the level could be toppish in the very short-term, the trend was up with 15.40 percent a possible target by the end of the week.
Foreigners were net buyers of 171.67 million rand's worth of South African bonds on Friday after buying 199.17 million on Thursday, the Bond Exchange said.
Nominal cumulative volumes were pegged at 607.96 million rand on Friday from 35.91 billion rand on Thursday -- settlement day.
On the forex market the rand ended a dull day around the day's weakest levels against a steady U.S. unit as dollar demand outweighed supply towards the end of trade.
At 1410 GMT the rand was at 4.4555/4585 versus the U.S. unit from 4.4530/4560 late on Friday after drifting gradually higher during the day on steady dollar demand.
"The rand could test slightly higher levels on Tuesday after the steady (dollar) demand that we saw coming through today," a forex trader at a leading local institution said.
Some dealers put the range for the week between 4.4350 to 4.4750, saying the market would take its cue from the dollar's performance and moves on the local bond market on Tuesday.
The dollar had last edged higher against the yen and the mark in sluggish U.S. trade with all eyes on the weak Dow Jones index after Friday's 148 point sell-off.
Against the crosses, the rand was last trading at 28.3279/3694 yen from 28.2963/3506 yen, 0.3863/3868 marks from 0.3868/3874 marks and 7.2282/2353 rand against sterling from 7.2321/2447.
On the money market, three-month deposit rates were quoted steady in a 16.60 to 16.65 percent offered range, while the 90-day BA rate was also unchanged at between 15.95 and 16.10 percent.
The Reserve Bank said South Africa's money market shortage eased to 8.175 billion rand on Saturday from 8.216 billion rand on Friday.
